paper.title: CAMK2D causes heart failure in mice with RBM20 cardiomyopathy
paper.evidentiaryLevel: mouse models (Rbm20 KO, Camk2d KO, DKO, Rbm20-p.Arg636Gln KI); pharmacological proof-of-principle with hesperadin in mice — do not imply human cure

shots.narration: Some families inherit an aggressive form of heart failure. It strikes early, and the heart can stop without warning.

shots.narration: One splicing target is the KY-nase cam-kay-two-dee. Does it drive the disease?
shots.onscreen: Does CAMK2D drive RBM20 heart failure?

shots.narration: To test that, researchers built mouse models: knockouts of R-B-M-twenty, of cam-kay-two-dee, and a double knockout of both.
They housed the animals in a research facility, then measured heart function by echo and challenged them for lethal arrhythmias.

shots.narration: In a knock-in disease model carrying a human mutation, they then tested a cam-kay-two inhibitor, hess-PAIR-uh-din.

shots.narration: Lose R-B-M-twenty alone, and the heart fails — the ventricle dilates, pumping collapses, and arrhythmias turn lethal.
shots.klingPrompt: Cinematic medical 3D render, a dilated mouse heart beating weakly and unevenly, the left chamber staying enlarged as the walls barely move with each labored cycle, locked-off camera at organ scale, dark clinical void, deep blue and teal palette with a faint deep-red cast, photoreal subsurface scattering, shallow depth of field, 16:9

shots.narration: Delete cam-kay-two-dee as well, and double-knockout mice were protected — better ejection fraction, less dilation, and far fewer deaths after an arrhythmia challenge.
Splicing of other R-B-M-twenty targets was still broken. So the rescue was not a general fix of splicing.
shots.klingPrompt: Cinematic medical 3D render, a mouse heart transitioning from a dilated weak chamber to a tighter stronger beat as the walls thicken slightly with each cycle, locked-off camera at organ scale, dark clinical void warming slightly toward amber, deep blue and teal palette, photoreal subsurface scattering, shallow depth of field, 16:9

shots.narration: Put any single cam-kay-two-dee splice variant back into the protected hearts, and dysfunction returned. Overactivation of the KY-nase — not which isoform — drove the failure.
In knock-in mice with a human disease mutation, daily hess-PAIR-uh-din restored ejection fraction within weeks, without clearing the mutant protein's cytoplasmic granules.
Phosphoproteomics confirmed it: cam-kay-two-dee activity rose with disease, and the drug dialed much of it back.

shots.narration: This is still mouse work — not a human trial. But it reframes R-B-M-twenty heart failure as something a selective cam-kay-two drug might treat.

shots.narration: Cause-directed therapy for this genetic cardiomyopathy is no longer only gene editing. Inhibiting the KY-nase cam-kay-two-dee is now a testable path.
